title: Method: one network for every decision, behaviour cloning then PPO with a league
text: Third method, deliberately unlike the GA (evolved rules) and az-v1 (tree search over buys): a 298-256-256-34 MLP answers all ~22 kinds of decision, imitates the GA genome first (1.08 M decisions, 98.5% agreement), then improves by PPO (clip 0.2, GAE lambda 0.95, entropy 0.01) against 40% GA base, 15% bots, 15% past snapshots, 30% itself. Runs in C inside the engine: 3 ms per game, so 3,000 games per ~10 s iteration.
rejected: more search (az-v1 showed it saturates); evolution again; a value-only method (DQN) — PPO is the standard, stable choice for a large discrete action space with masking

title: Iteration 100: level with az-v1's best agent after 25 minutes of RL
text: Goal checks against the GA base (az-v1's 1,000 goal games): 59.6% (iteration 25), 63.6% (50), 65.3% (75), 67.3% (100); the imitating network started at 52% in the evaluation games. Head to head against az-v1's best agent (net 357 + 400-simulation search, 1,000 fresh games): 49.2% (46.1-52.3%). The bot scores slid from 74.8% to 71.5%: it specialises against the GA genome, its most frequent opponent.

title: Built the AZ seat check: az-v1's best agent scores 69.7% on the same 1,000 goal games inside this engine build (az-v1 measured 70.2%), so the two projects' numbers compare directly.
